category: residential egress: rotating residential, prepaid GB packages

free_tier.stated: No free allowance published; 'Entry allowance 5 GB, Entry rate $2.75/GB, Payable total USD $13.75, Traffic validity 186 days'.
free_tier.notes: The 186-day validity is why this is the one metered product that could be bought in small amounts without losing the purchase at month end.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a byte stream, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable to the traffic; the purchased GB is valid for 186 days (5 GB package) or 31 days (packages from 10 GB)

egress.terms: Prepaid packages, each a fixed allowance at a fixed rate: '5 GB+ $13.75 $2.75/GB ... 10 GB $22.50 $2.25/GB ... 50 GB $87.50 $1.75/GB ... 150 GB $210.00 $1.40/GB ... 500 GB $475.00'. The product is 'a shared rotating pool, not a static ISP allocation'.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 0.95/GB at the 500 GB package (USD 475); the 1 TB package was not read

interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 rotating pool, country or continent selector, sticky sessions up to 120 minutes on the datacenter product; the residential page states connection-based rotation.
chaining: Prepaid and valid for 186 days at the entry tier, so it is the metered product a corpus can test once without a monthly commitment; at TiB scale it is still USD 973 for 500 GB.

limits.value: prepaid GB package; 500 GB for USD 475 is the largest package read
'Connection-based rotation; a fresh IP is not guaranteed' and sticky sessions up to 120 minutes

limits_note: Rotation per connection is the wrong shape for a long download: a single HTTP transfer holds one connection, so a rotation policy that only changes on a new connection leaves the transfer on one address, which is what a debrid IP check wants.

identity_cost.detail: Self-service checkout at app.databay.com with card; no identity document mentioned on the page read.

reliability_note: 'A fresh IP is not guaranteed for every connection' and sticky sessions 'may end before that requested window' - a mid-transfer address change is the failure mode, and it is the one debrid terms punish as account sharing.
confidence_note: The package table is on the vendor page read today. The 1 TB rung was below the fold and is not quoted, so the per-TiB figure is derived from the 500 GB package and labelled as such.

evidence.proved: the package ladder with rates and totals: 5 GB $2.75/GB ($13.75), 10 GB $2.25/GB ($22.50), 50 GB $1.75/GB ($87.50), 150 GB $1.40/GB ($210), 500 GB $475; and 'Entry starts at 5 GB' with 186-day validity

price_per_tb_month: USD 0.95/GB at the 500 GB package, i.e. USD 973 per TiB derived from that rung
notes: Entered as a low-rate outlier and stayed because of the 186-day validity, which makes it the only metered vendor here a small test purchase does not waste.

extras.validity: 186 days at 5 GB, 31 days from 10 GB
